Widget ink at indexed depths: grey grounds stay grey, muted recedes or dims (rich-unfiled-791c.yyzs)

Extra-high review of c048ae96b. terminal-contrast now runs every scene at
sixteen and 256 colors, with no terminal named and on the theme's own, and
caught each defect before the fix. A ground is the indexed slot that stands
for it, scored by deltaE_OK plus a cost for chroma it lacks, so a dark grey
never becomes VGA maroon or navy, and it is never written as the default.
No text is written in its ground's color. Muted text recedes: a slot other
than the default and its body text's, with less contrast than body text;
where none recedes and reads, it is body text with SGR dim. The fit's tint is
the intent's (textTint). The monochrome refusal leaves TerminalColors. Where
no slot reads, text is the most legible slot. Sorts are min-scans but for
the shades a fit reads on a miss; ground is hoisted out of the line map.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Widget ink reads the frame's terminal, holds a stated muted slot to its floor (rich-unfiled-791c.yyzs)

Medium review of 1c30a79ba. At an indexed depth a widget's pair is chosen
among the colors RenderOptions.terminal shows (resolveTerminal, as Effect
and ProgressBar do), and the muted slot is that terminal's: mutedSlot moves
to TerminalColors, validated 0-15, and a terminal whose sixteen are all its
foreground is refused. Grounds are never written as the default. The stated
slot is muted text's candidate at sixteen colors only, held to the floor and
handed to the fit on a miss. Receding from body text belongs to the intent
(recedesFrom in text-on.ts), so text-muted has it too. Slot OKLab is taken
once per terminal and depth.

BREAKING: WidgetBase.ground and ThemedWidget.disabledInk are functions of
the frame's drawing (colorSystem, terminal), not getters; a subclass
overriding either takes the argument.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Widget contrast is a setting, and sixteen colors draw the theme's own (rich-unfiled-791c.yyzs)

A themed widget takes `contrast`, the TextFit its text meets a floor with:
slide by default, TEXT_FITS.asIs to turn checking off, setContrast to change
it live. Widgets resolve colors at the frame's depth through one
ThemedWidget.ink; at an indexed depth a pair is written in the theme's own
sixteen rather than rounded against stock VGA, and muted text is the slot
each theme states (ThemePaletteData.ansiMuted, TerminalTheme.mutedSlot), so
a placeholder no longer looks typed at 16 colors. mutedInk owns the muted
look; a disabled TextInput's continuation marker is drawn disabled. The
contrast test names muted glyphs by scene, not by color.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
De-emphasized widget text is drawn in foreground-muted, held to its 3:1 floor, not terminal dim (rich-unfiled-791c.yyzs)
Ground runs read the census's line breaks through a lookahead, a test pins how a line feed meets each escape, and the hold bound says what it holds (rich-control-codes-xh4n.gux review)
The lexer reads ground text as runs, and an open escape carries its lexeme index on its state (rich-control-codes-xh4n.gux review)
An escape the bytes end inside stays on the line it began, and the lexer's string stops are osc8's (rich-control-codes-xh4n.gux review)

decodeAnsi reads its bytes in one VT500 lexing pass that the line split, the link reader and every escape consume (rich-control-codes-xh4n.gux)

A sequence a C0 control interrupts is now the sequence a terminal reads
wherever it is read: a NEL or CNL so interrupted ends the line, an OSC 8
an interrupted ESC introduces opens its link, and a CSI an ESC or C1
cancels draws nothing. A cut-off string is a lexeme of its own, so no
control can land in its payload; escapeTokens, INTERRUPTED and
OPEN_ESCAPE are gone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

A C0 control inside a CSI or an escape runs ahead of it and the sequence goes on, as a VT500 parser does (rich-control-codes-xh4n.8qs) (#589)

* A C0 control inside a CSI or an escape runs ahead of it and the sequence goes on, as a VT500 parser does (rich-control-codes-xh4n.8qs)

* A control inside a sequence runs in the tokenizer, after any string the sequence cuts off; a C0 break there ends the line and carries the sequence on (rich-control-codes-xh4n.8qs)

Replaces the executedFirst text rewrite, which moved a BEL or FF into a cut-off
string's payload. decodeLine now follows the rule too, and LF joins VT and FF.
Sequence patterns come from one builder; RUN_IN_SEQUENCE derives from ABORTS.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* A DEL inside a sequence is no token, so REP still repeats; a held break relocates by the census (rich-control-codes-xh4n.8qs)

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* A line break inside a sequence is left to the lexing pass (rich-control-codes-xh4n.gux); the carry linesOf held is removed (rich-control-codes-xh4n.8qs)
